html:
The treaty of 6 August 1861 by which Oba Dosunmu of Lagos ceded the island town to Britain, under threat of force, making it a British colony.

Ten years earlier the British had bombarded Lagos and replaced its king, Kosoko, saying they were ending the slave trade there. As a colony it grew into the main port of the region for palm oil, and freed Africans from Sierra Leone and Brazil settled in it. It became the base for British expansion inland and the capital of Nigeria until 1991. Lagos is now one of the largest cities in Africa. See also Lagos colony.
sum: The treaty of 6 August 1861 by which Oba Dosunmu of Lagos ceded the island town to Britain, under threat of force, making it a British colony.
